utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, would you like to continue with your witness, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, thank you. (redacted), recalled. Examined by MR. TIEGER, continued.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Good morning. (redacted), you are under oath. You understand you are still under oath, do you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. (To the witness): Good morning,

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Just before the adjournment yesterday, you were discussing the takeover of the transmitter at Lisina. Following the takeover of that transmitter, was there a change in the television broadcast which people at Prijedor could receive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What channel and from what area were people no longer able to receive television transmissions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The most important thing is that the population of Prijedor and Banja Luka had to watch on channel 2 of Sarajevo television what was sent from his Lisina transmitter, that is, on channel 2 they could only watch the news of the Belgrade television.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Previously what programmes had been available on Channel 2 through Sarajevo television?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On Channel 2 Sarajevo television alternately take over the news of television Belgrade and television Zagreb and a multi-ethnic programme called "Yutel".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was Yutel managed by people of different nationalities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Serbs, Muslims, Croats?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What kind of attitude did Yutel television take toward the war in Croatia, for example?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yutel was trying to contribute to peace and togetherness of the former Yugoslavia in all the ways possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sometime after the takeover of the transmitter Yutel was no longer available; is that right

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in the beginning we could see it now and then, and after a while it stopped completely, Yutel stopped completely.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You indicated that after that point only Belgrade TV was available on that channel. What kind of broadcasts came from Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have to say that one could also watch Sarajevo television on Channel 1. I am referring now to Channel 2 of Sarajevo television which regularly transmitted Belgrade prime time news, and on that channel they commenced very, very harsh propaganda directed against all other peoples of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you see extremist national leaders on Belgrade TV?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I saw Seselj, Arkan.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: For example, what was Seselj depicted doing on some of those broadcasts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Seselj attended several rallies. If I remember well, it was a rally in Vojvodina which is a region in Serbia and he spoke openly about what greater Serbia should look like. He listed the names of towns to belong there. He spoke about the threat to the Serb people, and other, the whole Serb people should live in one country. I saw him at a parade, at a review, where he attended a military parade.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did he participate in some way in that military parade either by meeting with officials or reviewing the troops?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he did meet them and, as far as I remember, he also met with Mrs. Bijeljina Plavsic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: With regard to his meeting with the troops, first of all, are we talking about the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they looked like JNA soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How did they respond to Seselj's presence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Quite normally, as if he was a high ranking politician.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did they salute him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You mentioned you also saw Arkan on TV with Mrs. Plavsic, I believe you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What were the two of them doing together?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were evidently very close -- "close" is perhaps not a good expression, but they seemed to have a friendly relationship.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was depicted on the footage you saw that indicated they had a friendly relationship?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I saw them greet each other and hug each other

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: During this time did you also have an opportunity to read periodicals and magazines from Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What themes appeared in those magazines or periodicals?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: More often than not what I found in those papers were supplements from the modern and more remote history of Serbia, mention of the battle on Kosovo, Dusan's empire as a state, a threat to the Serbs, criticisms for the falsified history about the Serbs, and very disagreeable, very unpleasant critique of the Croats, Slovenians, Muslims, Albanians.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did such promotion and dissemination of such themes appear to have an effect on relations between the national groups within Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What effect did it begin to have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Slowly people began to see, to look for, friends among their own ethnic group, that is, mistrust began to be created. This was politics; people began to support that kind of state of affairs, and others criticised that. But people who were good friends until that time began to mistrust one another.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did people begin to talk about each other or even report each other to authorities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know what period of time you have in mind before the takeover of power in Prijedor or after that, but after the takeover of power there were instances of that kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When we get to that point I will ask you specifically about that. Did the Serbian people within Prijedor begin to openly advocate the same views which were being espoused from Belgrade TV and through Belgrade media?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not so openly but there were some groups which did it openly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yesterday you also spoke about the difficulties which were occurring within the local assembly of Prijedor between the SDS and the SDA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to observe the last meeting that was held at the local assembly prior to the takeover?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was that a co-operative or harmonious meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was the main point of contention at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The main points of contention were the political order, political system, of Bosnia-Herzegovina, whether Bosnia-Herzegovina should remain in Yugoslavia, the army and the manager, the head of the public auditing service.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What position did SDS politicians take with respect to Prijedor's relationship with Yugoslavia or Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the position that was repeated many times before that, that the Serbs wanted to remain with their mother country Serbia, and to remain part of Yugoslavia even if rump -- that expression, that term "rump" was used very often.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did SDS politicians publicly proclaim support for greater Serbia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They manifested open support to remaining linked to the mother country, Serbia, but they did not refer to it as greater Serbia; often they said it was Yugoslavia, even if "rump".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you hear them refer to greater Serbia in private conversations or discussions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, often times they had their private debates and they would forget themselves and say, "We want it to remain a part of Serbia".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Had the SDS leadership indicated what it believed to be greater Serbia or Serbian land?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: SDS leadership kept pointing out what one could hear from Belgrade, all Serbs in one state, and I heard Mr. Karadzic saying that all the areas with at least five per cent of the Serb population were to be considered as Serb territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How did that last meeting of the assembly end?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It ended like many times before, very simply representatives of SDS proposed to withdraw, to go to their MP club, and that after a while they would notify about their decision and it lasted, well, perhaps more than an hour, and then they only said that they did not want to go on because not all matters had been cleared and that on some other occasion at some other session they would try to clarify it. So that that particular session was discontinued without a result.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is that the manner in which previous sessions had ended and were unable to achieve any kind of concrete results?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very often. It was almost a practice in the work of the assembly of the Prijedor municipality. There were almost always some excuses found why a session could not end, could not adjourn, in a normal way.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Excuse was found by whom or by which party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: During the period of time before the takeover, was there a discussion or discussions about separating Prijedor or dividing it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who proposed that Prijedor be divided?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How did they propose to divide Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They proposed to divide it according to what they had found in Cadaster registers, and they announced that 70 per cent of Prijedor territory belonged to Serbs, and they even published a map of their division in Prijedor, that is, in Prijedor municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This was a map of the proposed division of Prijedor for Serbs in one part and Muslims in another?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What part of Prijedor was allocated to the Muslim community?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Muslim community would get the outskirts of the town where more Muslims lived, such as old towns, Stari Grad, Rizvanovici, Kozarac, etc., and the central part the town of Prijedor itself, all the institutions and almost all industries would go to the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How did the Muslim community respond to the proposal by the SDS that Prijedor be divided so that the Serbs received the industry or most of the industry and most of the institutions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they responded diversely, of course. They tried to prevent it in a way, and even the SDA President, Mirza Mujadzic, suggested in a public broadcast that the areas of Prijedor, Sanski Most, Bosanski Novi and Kljuc remain a neutral zone, a zone of peace, that would not belong either to the Serb or to the Muslim entity.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did the national groups in Prijedor live in such a way that a division in Prijedor could be achieved simply by drawing an arbitrary or theoretical line through the opstina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What would be the result of any proposal to have Muslims in one area and Serbs in another?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Terrible effect would ensue because we lived together, we lived in the same houses, we married, we took wives or husbands from other ethnic groups, we had children, we were friends and would be the same as to divide one body, one soul.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was there also discussion about establishing a separate Police Force?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did that discussion involve Serbian officials from outside the opstina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you recall any particular Serbian official from outside Prijedor who came in to participate in the discussions about the possibility of a separate Police Force?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I remember it well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was Mr. Stojan Zupljanin, chief of the regional district of Banja Luka in charge of security.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do the decisions by the Prijedor police have to go through the CSB or the security office in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know their organisation, but I assume that the main centre was Sarajevo. However, I am not sure if Prijedor had to be under the Banja Luka patronage.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When Mr. Zupljanin came over from Banja Luka, did he come with the apparent authority to resolve the issue of separate police on behalf of the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I assume he did have such authority which normally I did not see, but as everybody received him, accepted him and accepted help from him, it is natural to assume that he did have the authority to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who had proposed separate police departments or Police Forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know exactly who was the person who had proposed it, but about a month or two before the takeover of power there was plenty of discussion in the police station, that is, Prijedor SUP, about this and I know it well that they held joint meeting altogether in the police station at SUP and that they decided to go on as one, as joint Police Force.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who announced that decision?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was announced on the radio and in the paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who made the decision publicly on behalf of the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On behalf of the Serbs, I do not know who decided that, that is, to keep the joint police before the arrival of Mr. Zupljanin, but the public was told that it had been agreed within the Prijedor SUP to keep the joint Police Force.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were they told that after Mr. Zupljanin came from Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before Mr. Zupljanin, but when Mr. Zupljanin came it was repeated again.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You mentioned yesterday the plebiscite which was held in November 1991. Was that plebiscite regarded by local SDS officials as an important event?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was the reason for that, what was the plebiscite's importance to local SDS officials?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, at the time Yugoslavia as a state was already facing imminent columns, Slovenia, Croatia. The foundations of the former Yugoslavia were already shattered and now there remained the problem of Bosnia. SDS wanted to ensure the support of the people to join the mother country Serbia, that is, to remain in the so-called rump Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were the results of the plebiscite cited or focused on by Serbian officials when separate institutions by Serbs were later created?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: (redacted), I would like to bring you to the period of time immediately before the takeover of Prijedor. First of all, I would like to ask you about the extent of military presence in Prijedor at that time. Were you aware of military forces in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and that was a very important fact, this military presence at Prijedor. I knew that in Prijedor at the airfield at Urije there was a unit that had been located there -- we called it the units from Pancevo of the JNA, a unit of the JNA -- and we heard that a missile unit was located at Kozara. The war in Croatia, in Pakrac and Lipik, and almost all the people who were armed then who went to that war, they would be coming back home bringing arms with them. The atmosphere in the town was very bad, so that we felt that we were under some kind of silent occupation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was the ethnic composition of those troops?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that a very small number of Muslims and Croats had accepted the call for mobilization and to go to war to Pakrac and Lipik. So we can conclude from that, as far as I know the people from Prijedor and the situation there, that a very high percentage, an enormous percentage -- I could not tell you the exact percentage -- that was practically a Serb army.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you said that "we felt we were under some kind of silent occupation", who did you mean by "we"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, of course, I mean the Bosniaks and the Croats and the other people who are not Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Does "Bosniaks" refer to the Muslim community?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You mentioned the Pancevo unit that Urije airport, what kind of unit was this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not really an expert of military things, but I could see that was a tank unit. I know what a tank is. I was going through a street after they had arrived at Urije and on a tarmac road you could still see damage that had been made after the mechanized part of the tanks passed, these mechanized units, and the mud; everything that a normal person, an average person, who is not a soldier could notice to know what things were going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You also mentioned that soldiers who returned from the war in Croatia retained their weapons and were in the town. What was the nature of their behaviour when they got to town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very arrogant, very arrogant. I felt in the town an almost military atmosphere. They would be coming back home for a rest and then go back there in certain intervals. They would shoot after each goal at a match. They would wound people, civilians, by chance. Even in the part where I lived, there was a primary school, a child had been injured there and a man who was standing at his balcony, they used machine guns to shoot out of the windows. They were showing off the force.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In addition to the JNA troops in the locations you mentioned and returned Reservists, were other Serbs in opstina Prijedor armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not there was any effort to arm Serb civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know, concretely.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you observe such an effort?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was that in your neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What did you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My colleague was sitting at my place on the 6th or 7th April 1992, we were expecting the news about the recognition of Bosnia as a state. He came back. I was looking through the window of my flat. I saw a truck full of arms. I saw people who would come and take those arms, and I very concretely saw (redacted), my neighbour, who took an automatic weapon and put it under his coat.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What national group did your neighbour belong to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What national group did the others who came to take arms from the truck belong to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were other Muslims in your neighbourhood also aware of the distribution of arms to Serb civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. They were observing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What impact did that have on the Muslims in your neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A very terrible impact; fear, helplessness, completely lost.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Around this time did you begin hearing the use of offensive terms regarding Muslims used in public and in the media?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time, not in the local media, I could not hear it that often, but I could hear and read it in other media where we, the Muslims, were always called "Turks".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What did that term connote when it was used in the media?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is very easy to conclude if you take all the time into account, the constant syndrome that we, Muslims, have, the syndrome of Turks, they were constantly repeating about the Kosovo battle, the Czar Dusan and the Prince Lazer and carrying around about symbols of Prince Lazer, and all the preparations for the 600th anniversary of the Serb battle, and the Turks are presented as the people who kill; and if we were called the "Turks", it is not very difficult to conclude what they mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You mentioned the presence of the army in Prijedor. Who was the Commander or Commanders of the army units in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that Mr. Radmilo Zeljaja and Mr. Radmilo Arsic were that. Those were two persons that participated in the public life and I cannot tell you who was the real Commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did either one of them have a connection to any of the local political parties?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, one could say that people like Mr. Radmilo Zeljaja were more close to the SDS party; whereas Mr. Arsic would more often come to the meeting of the assembly of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Would Arsic speak at the meetings of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot recall that because I was not a member. You could ask somebody else, but I can suppose that he did take part.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did he also associate with members of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, maybe he could, but Radmilo Zeljaja did it more than he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You have mentioned the takeover of Prijedor several times. Do you remember the date of that event?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 30th April 1992, it was a Thursday.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: About what time of the day did you first discover that the takeover had taken place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On that day at 6.10.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was it that you saw or heard that alerted you to the fact that something had happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What nationality were these soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serb nationality.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were they JNA soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were dressed in various ways. People wearing military uniforms with or without a helmet, camouflage uniforms. They had ranks, some had insignia over their pockets, and they wore armed bands of different colours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: With what title?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Stakic explain on the radio what had happened and ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: -- and what the SDS intended to do with Prijedor thereafter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What did he explain?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He said that, among other things, the Serbs could not tolerate any more such atmosphere without work and such discord, so they decided to take the power in their hands. Upon the question, "What would happen to Muslims?" he answered, "They do not interest us. Their territories, those territories that belong to Muslims and the municipality of Prijedor can be organised and managed in the way they decide. We are only interested in our areas".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: At that point had the Serb military forces taken control of all the institutions in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All the institutions from police, the town hall, industrial plants, radio, communications, the bakery, the medical centre, the bank, the public auditing office, traffic -- everything of vital importance for the life in the municipality of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In addition to the soldiers you mentioned earlier, did you see heavy equipment or heavy arms in Prijedor that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: At what time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was on 2nd May. We were watching a tank unit that was passing through the street Sava Kovacevic, and then they continued through the JNA street across the bridge on the Sana towards Sanski Most, and then we heard that it had been located in Lusci.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you see any heavy artillery?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, tanks with canons. I cannot tell you anything about calibres or the names of these weapons, but there were tanks and canons. The whole part of town was resounding while they were passing through it. It was a very, very long column.
